section_summary: This section finishes an earlier paper on relief during the occupation of Japan, then contains a July 7, 1945 memorandum and a longer draft on the same subject. The papers discuss minimum diets, Japanese responsibility for food distribution, and possible needs for imported supplies and transport. The section ends with a brief comment on the draft, a citizen’s proposal for Japan’s rehabilitation, and the State Department’s reply.

subfiles.title: Relief policy paper, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Recommendations on the minimum living conditions and supplies needed during the occupation of Japan.
subfiles.summary: The paper estimates initial diets of 1,200 calories to prevent starvation and about 1,600 to prevent disease and unrest. It considers possible imports, especially transport, fertilizer, textiles, sugar, soybeans and salt, while placing primary responsibility for production and distribution on the Japanese. Its recommendations call for monitoring disease rates, limiting gratuitous distribution, supporting controls on supplies, and encouraging movement from food deficit areas.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding draft paper on relief policy for Japan
subfiles.about: Kahn forwards a draft relief policy paper and explains its preparation.
subfiles.summary: Kahn forwards a draft reviewed with Martin and seeks agreement on its approach before final revision.

subfiles.title: Policy with Respect to Relief (Japan)
subfiles.about: Proposed United States military government policy for relief in Japan after hostilities.
subfiles.summary: The draft defines relief chiefly as imported supplies needed to prevent starvation or disease and unrest that would impede military government. It examines uncertain stocks, war damage, transport, the capacity of Japanese administration, and possible imports over both short and longer periods. Its conclusions favor Japanese production and equitable distribution, propose tentative diets of 1,200 and 1,500 calories, and give allied and liberated peoples priority for scarce supplies.

subfiles.title: Wilcox’s comment on the relief memorandum
subfiles.about: Wilcox comments briefly on Kahn’s occupation and relief memoranda.
subfiles.summary: Wilcox agrees with Kahn’s occupation views and calls the relief memorandum a useful start.

subfiles.title: Letter to the President proposing Japan’s rehabilitation
subfiles.about: A citizen proposes an educational and economic approach to Japan’s rehabilitation.
subfiles.summary: The handwriting and OCR are difficult to read. The letter appears to propose educating Japanese people in democratic ideas and making Japan agriculturally self supporting; it also mentions silk production and asks the President for a response.

subfiles.title: Reply to E. A. Anderson
subfiles.from: J. M. Colton Hand, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges Anderson’s rehabilitation proposal.
subfiles.summary: The department thanks Anderson for the proposal forwarded by the White House.
